transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-05-09 14:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Zephyr CTO), Samir Khan (ML Engineer), Maya Lopez (SRE lead)
Links shared: benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood.app/benchmarks/zephyrai-2025), security docs (s3://redwood/sec/zephyr)

Summary: quick POC scoping to agree success criteria for latency and throughput, define TTFT vs TPOT targets at p95/p99, and map out benchmark runs and timeline. Zephyr wants to validate 2 use cases (chat assistant for internal docs and an API summarizer) with expected request sizes and 2 wk pilot.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing (tokens, QPS), measurement plan (warm vs cold, synthetic vs replay), metrics (TTFT time-to-first-token, TPOT time-per-output-token, p95/p99, error rate), hardware choices, timeline and next steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maria (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm maria, i'll run the commercial side, arjun here will own the technical plan.
[00:12] Arjun (Redwood SE): hi all. today's goal is to come out with a concrete SLO definition and a measurement plan we can run in the POC. we'll cover TTFT vs TPOT and how we measure p95/p99.
[00:28] Lena (Zephyr CTO): good, we want concrete numbers — our product team cares about first token for UX in the chat flows and per-token cost for bulk summarization.
[00:40] Samir (ML Eng): quick context: two primary flows — 1) internal chat agent, median input ~64 tokens, expected output ~128 tokens, baseline traffic 30 QPS with 2x peaks at 60 QPS for business hours; 2) summarization API: median input ~512 tokens, output ~256 tokens, lower QPS ~8 steady with spikes to 20.
[01:10] Maya (SRE): add that cold starts are very sensitive — a small percentage of cold containers cause elevated p99, so we need both warm steady-state and cold-start measurements. also, we need to test in VPC with our NAT/proxy to reflect network egress.
[01:32] Arjun: great. let's define terms so we're aligned. TTFT here = time from request arrival at Redwood-ingress to first token emitted back to client (end-to-end). TPOT = time per output token after first token — effectively the incremental latency per generated token, measured across streaming tokens (avg/median and p95/p99).
[02:10] Lena: is TPOT the same as "time per token" or is it amortized with batching?
[02:16] Arjun: good question. we'll measure both single-request TPOT (no batching) and batch-amortized TPOT at planned batching configs. for POC we should report: TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT p50/p95/p99 (single-request), and TPOT amortized at target batch sizes (e.g., batch=8,16) because our summarizer might batch requests.
[02:48] Samir: what targets should we aim for? in production now with their self-hosted setup, we see TTFT p95 ~420ms and p99 ~750ms for chat; cost is high and GPU utilization low.
[03:03] Maria: Zephyr's target UX is visibly snappy — internal goal is TTFT p95 <= 120 ms for chat, p99 <= 300 ms; summarization flow is less strict: TTFT p95 <= 300 ms, p99 <= 700 ms. TPOT targets: chat TPOT p95 <= 12 ms/token, p99 <= 30 ms/token; summarizer TPOT p95 <= 15 ms/token, p99 <= 40 ms/token. these are initial asks, we can iterate.
[03:40] Lena: those chat numbers sound aggressive compared to our baseline but worth testing. do you have examples of model variants or quantization that get you close?
[03:51] Arjun: yes — we recommend a few variants: FP16 on A100/H100, int8 quantized on inference-optimized kernels, and a small batch on H100 for lower per-token. we'll include a matrix with expected per-token numbers and cost per million tokens.
[04:10] Maya: we need measurement discipline — define warm vs cold: warm = model already loaded on GPU and KV cache primed with 1 preceding token in session; cold = model load + warm-up overhead. report both separately.
[04:26] Arjun: agreed. measurement plan (high level): 1) run a 30-minute warm steady-state workload replay (replay of customer trace) to measure TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99; 2) run a 5-10 minute cold-start burst test with container restarts to capture p99 cold behaviors; 3) run batching experiments (batch sizes 1, 8, 16) for the summarizer; 4) capture GPU utilization, memory, error rates, and token throughput (tokens/sec) and end-to-end QPS. we'll also measure prefix/KV cache hit effects by toggling session caching.
[05:10] Samir: for the traffic trace we'll provide one hour of production-ish data (anonymized) covering business hours and off-peak. can you replay that with the same inter-arrival times?
[05:21] Arjun: yes we'll do time-preserving replay in our harness. we'll annotate which requests are cold vs warm.
[05:30] Lena: what's the minimum sample size to get reliable p99 for TTFT?
[05:34] Arjun: p99 stability depends on traffic volume; rule of thumb — for p99 you want thousands of requests. with your 1 hour trace at 30 QPS average that's ~108k requests; that's more than enough. for shorter tests we'll boot more parallel clients to hit required sample size.
[05:55] Maria: what about error budgets and SLO pass/fail logic for the POC?
[05:58] Arjun: propose this: pass if for the chat flow TTFT p95 <= 120ms AND TTFT p99 <= 300ms OR we hit cost target with TTFT p95 <= 180ms; basically two acceptance paths: (A) latency-first path, (B) cost-first path with tolerances. additionally require no functional regressions in output quality (>1% drop on evaluation prompts).
[06:30] Maya: we also want to measure tail at the network layer — egress thru our VPC sometimes adds ~30-50ms. include a variant of the test with VPC-proxied traffic.
[06:42] Arjun: noted. we'll run each benchmark with direct-hosted networking and through your VPC proxy to capture extra network tail.
[06:55] Samir: let's talk sizing — what GPU counts should we expect for 30 QPS chat with median 128 output tokens?
[07:02] Arjun: rough back-of-envelope: if TPOT amortized is 12 ms/token at batch1, a single GPU can do tokens/sec = ~83 (1/0.012) per stream but concurrency matters; we'll compute requirement using per-request tokens (128) * QPS (30) * token-time to get required token throughput. but for planning, recommend starting with 2 dedicated A100s for pilot, or 1 H100 depending on model and quantization. we'll run sizing numbers in the spreadsheet.
[07:40] Lena: timeline? we want POC within two weeks and a pilot in production after.
[07:46] Maria: propose schedule: this week finish benchmark plan & sample trace (due Fri 5/14), next week run benchmarks (5/19–5/23) and present results in a 60-minute review. then decisions on Dedicated vs Hosted.
[07:59] Arjun: technical notes we'll capture in the benchmark doc: - measurement endpoints instrumented at ingress/egress to capture TTFT accurately - stream-level timing where first-token timestamp and each token timestamp recorded - measure CPU/GPU counters, NVTX traces for any kernel stalls - record KV cache hit rates and lookups per session.
[08:25] Maya: we need role-based access to the result sheets and logs; can you add our SRE group?
[08:30] Maria: yes, i'll share drive links and set permissions for the Zephyr SRE group.
[08:36] Lena: one more on quality — we want to ensure generation quality isn't sacrificed. how will you measure that?
[08:42] Arjun: we'll include an eval harness that runs a fixed set of prompts and computes automated metrics (perplexity/delta logprob, ROUGE on summaries, and a small human spot-check). target is <1% drop vs your baseline model on the eval set; if quality drops, we'll annotate whether it's due to quantization or routing to smaller model.
[09:05] Samir: any gotchas with KV cache and multi-turn chat?
[09:09] Arjun: yes: KV cache priming affects TTFT — if cache is warm, first token can be much faster because less compute on prefix. we'll run scenarios with full prefix caching, partial, and cold. document will show separate numbers.
[09:26] Lena: competitors — we've run some tests against our OpenAI hosted infra and saw better latency but much higher costs. want to validate Redwood's cost/latency tradeoffs.
[09:36] Maria: okay we'll include competitor baseline numbers in the spreadsheet where you can paste your OpenAI/AWS numbers for apples-to-apples.
[09:43] Arjun: measurement outputs we'll provide: CSV of raw timestamps, a dashboard with TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, errors, and an executive summary that maps to the success criteria.
[09:58] Maya: please include a measurement of tail-degrading events (GC, OOM, network flaps) and note mitigation e.g., autoscale, fallback models.
[10:06] Arjun: will do. also note we'll test fallback policies — route to next-best model if latency spikes or capacity constrained — and measure impact on latency and quality.
[10:20] Maria: let's recap next steps...
[10:22] Maria: (recap) 1) Redwood shares benchmark plan & sheet (Maria/Arjun) 2) Zephyr shares traffic trace + eval prompts (Samir) 3) Confirm VPC window (Maya) 4) Run benchmarks week of 5/19 and review results.
[10:40] Lena: makes sense, thanks. excited to see numbers.
[10:45] Maria: thanks all, we'll follow up via email w/ calendar invite for benchmark kickoff.
[10:50] Meeting ends

Notes on measurement definitions (extracted for clarity):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): measured at ingress to first byte of token emitted to client. report in ms at p50/p95/p99.
- TPOT (time-per-output-token): incremental time between consecutive tokens after first token; report single-request TPOT and batch-amortized TPOT. units ms/token at p50/p95/p99.
- Warm steady-state: model already loaded and session cache behavior representative of production. Run 30-minute steady replay.
- Cold-start: measure from empty worker pool + model load; run short bursts with container restarts.
- Batching configs: test batch sizes 1, 8, 16. report amortized TPOT and throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU.
- Success criteria: chat TTFT p95 <= 120ms & p99 <= 300ms OR cost-first path (TTFT p95 <= 180ms with target cost savings). summarizer TTFT p95 <= 300ms p99 <= 700ms. quality drop <=1% on eval metrics.

Benchmark deliverables:
- Raw timestamp CSVs and replay script
- Summary dashboard (TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, errors)
- Cost model: per-M token cost by model/hardware/quantization
- Recommendations: model variant, batching, cache policy, routing policy, and pilot sizing

End of transcript.
